criteria.idempotent_open: Check carrier authentication plus nonce freshness, then run the state machine purely by delivery_id: a done row replays done, a dead row replays dead, an unknown id 404s, and failures stay pending with a durable attempt row. No lease-ownership test. Converges because downstream receivers deduplicate by delivery_id and no transition ever un-delivers a row.
criteria.ownership_checked: Require the acknowledging worker to still hold the lease (worker_id plus version match) before applying the ack, else 409 lease_lost. Stale-holder and post-expiry acknowledgements must reclaim first. Tighter attribution at the cost of more 409 arms and extra companion reclaim handling.

ack.instructions: Should the carrier acknowledgement require current lease ownership, or authenticate the carrier and apply idempotently by delivery id?

criteria.multi_batch: Return up to K rows per claim inside one transaction via a recursive claim loop, each row under the same lease/version rules. Fewer round trips, but recursion inside the decision needs per-level assertion mocks and a larger decision surface.
criteria.single_page: Return zero or one row per claim: oldest claimable row via lookup-first SELECT plus conditional UPDATE on version. Straight-line Can with mechanical assertions; the companion pages until empty and retries spurious race empties. Batching lives companion-side.

claim.instructions: Should one claim request take several rows at once, or take a single row while the companion pages?

criteria.bearer_nonce: Send the shared secret as a bearer header; freshness comes from a timestamp plus a unique nonce. Simplest Can code and no per-request signature. A captured request inside the skew window is still nonce-blocked, but body tampering in transit has no cryptographic binding and the design leans on loopback/trusted scope plus deployment transport security.
criteria.body_fields: Put timestamp_ms and nonce inside each signed JSON body; the signature header carries HMAC-SHA-256 of the exact body bytes and a second header carries the protocol version. Reuses the proven provider verification shape with no canonical-string assembly. Any tampered field breaks the signature; replays die on the unique nonce insert.
criteria.header_canonical: Send timestamp, nonce and signature as headers; the signature covers a joined canonical string of timestamp, nonce, method, path and body text. Binds routing plus body, at the cost of canonical assembly and header parsing in Can. Replays die on the nonce table.

envelope.instructions: Which carrier authentication envelope best fits the decided guarantees and Can constraints?

state.constraints: Can ships HMAC-SHA-256 over exact bytes (proven on the provider path), JSON bodies with byte limits, integer arithmetic and ordering, text::join for canonical strings, JSON integer timestamps with a wall clock, transactions with conditional UPDATE plus affected-row counts, and a unique-nonce table. Descriptors admit SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only, RETURNING-free. Single-row decisions are straight-line; multi-row needs recursion with per-level assertion mocks. String compare is exact but not constant-time (documented limit).
state.criteria: Prefer the smallest mechanism that closes R16-03, keeps at-least-once plus idempotent ack airtight under two racing workers, survives supervisor restart with zero Can-side recovery beyond idempotency, stays assertion-friendly, and reports honest versioned failures over the C-E status contract.
state.decided: P09-B3 fixes claim as lease-table rows taken by a lookup-first claim_outbox(worker_id, lease_until) transaction with no locking-read dependency; worker identity, lease expiry and heartbeat ride in the protocol version; delivery is at-least-once with idempotent ack plus the C-C unknown-write vocabulary; after N protocol-versioned attempts the companion marks the row through a dead_letter endpoint while Can owns the dead-letter table and decide_ack dead-letter rules; supervisor restart redelivers unacked rows. F-R11-04 retains loopback plus trusted-carrier scope. No external users and no backwards compatibility; secrets arrive via environment only.
state.goal: Implement task F05, the authenticated Can/companion webhook pair: Can owns the ledger, outbox, attempts, idempotent decide/ack transactions and commit-unknown reconciliation; the companion owns claims, delivery, retry scheduling, bounded concurrency, poison handling, crash recovery and destination policy enforcement. Carrier endpoints must authenticate (the R16-03 fix): unauthenticated, replayed and invalid carrier requests reject.
state.threats: An attacker may replay captured carrier requests, tamper with bodies in transit, or run a second worker racing legitimate claims. Lease races must converge without double business effects; duplicate deliveries downstream are absorbed by delivery_id deduplication, never by assuming single delivery. Secrets stay in environment snapshots and never in logs; responses use the C-E status contract (200/400/401/404/409/413/503, every case with a body).
